cuts.moves: From handleKeyPress (1075-1214, ~140 lines). Two parts. (a) The ORDERED modal chain at the top (menu, dialogue.onKey, component guide, inventory, trade, social, quest log, station...) is order-sensitive and swallows keys: keep it as an explicit ordered array `MODAL_CHAIN: Array<{ isOpen:()=>boolean; onKey:(code)=>void|boolean }>` built in one place, NOT an unordered registry (guide Gotcha: order matters). Each entry is a small object {isOpen, close, closeKeys:['Escape','KeyI']}. (b) The global keys that follow the chain become a Record<string /*default code*/, (ctx)=>void> action table, e.g. KeyC, KeyM, KeyN, KeyI, KeyL, KeyK, KeyP, F2, F3, F4, KeyR, ... each entry carrying its own guard (loggedIn, !systemMapUI.isOpen, proto). Add an invariant test: every ActionDef.id in input/keybindings.ts ACTIONS whose default key is handled by Game has a table entry, or is on an allowlist of keys read in tickInput.
cuts.risk: Medium. Behaviour depends on ordering and on early `return`s that swallow keys; a table lookup must run AFTER the whole modal chain. Also the dispatch is a Record lookup instead of an if-chain, so keys with a conditional fall-through (C ignored on the map, Esc priority) need the guard inside the entry to return false so later entries still get a chance. Per-keypress, not per-tick, so perf is irrelevant.

tokenEstimate: About 0.9M to 1.4M tokens total. Input-fields cut about 100k; inputSend about 250k (reads the 210-line function repeatedly, plus the replay test); keys about 150k; serverMessages about 300k (400 lines to move plus the host interface); windows registry about 300k (the largest rename surface); doc updates and review about 120k. Wall time roughly 3 to 4 sequential agent-runs if the middle three go in parallel.
hazards: Prediction drift: tickInput feeds both network.send and state.applyInput/predictTick. Any change to which fields go in the message, their quantisation (dequantizeCursorAngle, CURSOR_DIST_STEP), the seq order, or the send-vs-predict branch desyncs the local ship from the server. Neutral input must keep helm and brace as they were (comment in sendNeutralInput). The server side (applyInputToEntity) re-quantises targetAngle with replicaAngle; do not touch it while refactoring the field loop.

Input list inconsistency already present: the linger line (GameServer ~2843) and the dock line (~3292) zero only 10 keys and omit brace and dodge, while releaseControls zeroes brace and dodge but not helm. The shared list will change one of these behaviours. Decide explicitly per site (INPUT_HELD vs INPUT_ALL) and test it; do not silently unify.

Input byte format is full (flags2 in protocol.ts ~1155 is out of bits). The shared list must NOT drive bit packing; leave binary layout and wireHash.ts sample frame alone, or the pinned hash and PROTOCOL_VERSION must be bumped with npm run wire:bump.

Circular imports: the new app/* modules must import Game types with `import type` only and receive everything through small host interfaces. windows.ts imports ~74 UI modules; if any UI module imports from Game.ts (some pass `Game` types for callbacks) a cycle appears, which the bundler tolerates until a top-level use. Check with a madge-style grep or the build.

serverOutOfMain: moving imports between files can pull server/src code (via sandbox, replays, ship economy) into the start-up chunk. Keep lazy `import()` calls and the Lazy<T> wrappers intact and run npm run build:client after every cut.

Concurrent edits: every cut edits Game.ts. Other agents (HUD chips, new windows, new keybindings per the guide's 'How to extend' steps) also edit the field block, init() and handleKeyPress. Announce a freeze on Game.ts, or sequence the cuts and rebase immediately; do not use git checkout/restore/stash/reset (project rule, large uncommitted tree). The guide's line ranges (1075-1214, 1478-1688, 1722-2121, 436-665) will be wrong after the first merge, so tell each agent to grep symbols, not line numbers.

Per-tick perf: tickInput runs every tick and handleServerMessage('snapshot') runs at tick rate. Do not allocate arrays, closures, spreads or Object.entries in these paths; reuse the sample/message objects; handler table must be a plain object keyed by type (monomorphic lookup), not a Map of wrapped closures built per message. domWrite (setText/setHtml) rules still apply for per-frame DOM.

Key order and swallowing: the modal chain relies on early return. Converting to a table can let a later key fire while a window is open, or stop Esc closing the topmost window. Keep the chain ordered and test it. Rebinding: handlers must keep matching DEFAULT codes; never use bound keys or hard-coded letters in hint text.

Proto mode (?proto, ProtoHooks): several windows and handlers are skipped with `if (!this.proto)`, and the input path uses targetTick: undefined and skips applyInput in proto. Both paths must keep working; proto has no prediction.

Handler coverage: today unhandled ServerMessage types fall through the switch silently. A typed table makes the gaps visible; allowlist the intentionally ignored types (and those consumed by shipClient.handleMessage) rather than adding no-op handlers.
Brood Mother, Fly.io leftover and the hazards.json comment noted by the guide writers are unrelated; do not fix them in these cuts.
